title: Zone pairing failure with abnormal AMR routing or roster state
user_facing_summary: Use when a site reports that a zone cannot obtain a pair, AMRs are not behaving as expected, or replacement AMRs are routing to the hospital instead of supporting the affected workflow.
playbook_goal: Confirm the observable pairing and fleet symptoms, determine whether the affected AMR roster or mapping state is abnormal, guide an authorized site-side isolation or removal decision when supported, and validate that normal operation returns.
observed_entry_symptoms: A zone is unable to get a pair.
The ACB workflow is reported as down or unable to operate.
Replacement AMRs route to the hospital lane instead of supporting the affected zone.
An AMR is reported with low battery or is physically under a rack.
The site reports that AMR behavior remains abnormal after an attempted replacement.
negative_or_absent_signals: The source does not provide a confirmed service crash, API failure, or database error.
The source does not independently confirm that low battery was the current cause; one support message described it as a possible initiating condition rather than the current cause.
The RMS screenshot details are not sufficiently legible to establish exact status fields or error codes.
Recovery was reported by site communication and short monitoring, not independently confirmed by readable live telemetry.
support_user_language_examples: Nothing is pairing in the zone
AMRs are going to the hospital
The replacement robots keep going to hospital
We have a low-battery robot under the rack
The robots were removed and added but it still isn't working
The fleet is not taking tasks
tentative_internal_patterns: Possible abnormal robot roster or mapping state after remove/add activity
Possible unassigned or unmapped AMR affecting pairing or task assignment
Possible residual physical or location state involving an AMR unable to reach charging
Possible routing or workflow diversion toward the hospital lane
internal_pattern_notes: These are tentative patterns from support discussion and case resolution text. The source does not establish a confirmed root cause. The low-battery condition may have initiated the issue, while the later suspected pattern involved robot removal, addition, or mapping state.
separability_reason: The reported low battery, hospital routing, RMS roster concern, robot removal, and monitoring all address the same goal: restore zone pairing and normal AMR task behavior. They are not sufficiently independent to justify multiple candidates.
confidence_reason: The packet contains a clear observable symptom pattern, a named RMS surface, repeated discussion of remove/add and mapping state, a source-supported site-side recovery action, and reported post-action stability. Confidence is limited because the RMS details are partly unreadable, the recovery was narrative rather than independently verified, and the source uses inconsistent ACB/ECB naming.
